# SDDL conformance corpus — the cases libpeios and libp-go must agree on.
#
# Peios has two SDDL implementations at opposite ends of one pipeline:
# libp-go compiles a recipe's SDDL in `pekit` and `peipkg pack`, and libpeios
# parses it in `seed-sd`, peinit and the `sd` command. A descriptor an author
# tests with `sd` has to pack, and a descriptor the Go side emits has to
# re-parse on the Rust side. PEI-562 is what happens when they drift.
#
# CANONICAL COPY
#   libpeios/src/security/sddl/testdata/sddl-conformance.txt
#
# DUPLICATED, BYTE FOR BYTE, IN
#   libp-go/sddl/testdata/sddl-conformance.txt
#
# The two live in separate git repositories that reach each other only as
# version-pinned published artefacts, so a genuinely shared file would have to
# come from a third repository both vendor — more machinery than the corpus is
# worth. They are copies instead, and each side's test asserts the revision
# line below, so updating one and not the other fails the other's suite rather
# than passing quietly. Edit the canonical copy, copy it across, bump the
# revision in both, and update REVISION in:
#   libpeios/src/security/sddl/grammar/tests.rs
#   libp-go/sddl/conformance_test.go
#
# revision: 1
#
# FORMAT
#   One case per line. Fields are separated by a single TAB. Blank lines and
#   lines beginning with `#` are ignored.
#
#   rights <field> <mask>
#       Parsing the ACE rights field <field> yields <mask>, written as eight
#       lowercase hex digits with an `0x` prefix. Parse direction only:
#       formatting a mask is deliberately different on the two sides (libp-go
#       always emits hex because mnemonics are object-class-dependent and
#       lossy; libpeios decomposes into mnemonics), and neither is wrong.
#
#   sid <alias> <sid>
#       The two-letter SID alias <alias> parses to <sid>, AND formatting <sid>
#       emits <alias>. Both directions, because this is the round trip that
#       PEI-562 was filed for: a descriptor the Go side formats with an alias
#       the Rust side has never heard of does not re-parse at all. Every SID
#       here is distinct, so the mapping is a bijection and the two formatters
#       cannot disagree about which alias to choose.
#
#   badrights <field>
#       The rights field <field> is rejected by both parsers. The message is
#       not compared — only that neither accepts it.

# --- Rights fields --------------------------------------------------------
#
# The mixed form is the one PEI-562 was filed about. /tmp's descriptor needs
# FILE_ADD_FILE|FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY, which have no two-letter mnemonic, so
# the natural spelling is a mnemonic set plus 0x6. Writing the whole mask as
# bare hex is correct and says nothing.

rights	FRFX0x6	0x001200af
rights	0x1200af	0x001200af

# The same field with a hex tail that supplies no bits the mnemonics did not:
# all three of these are the plain mnemonic mask.
rights	FRFX	0x001200a9
rights	FRFX0x0	0x001200a9
rights	FRFX0x80	0x001200a9

# Uppercase `0X` is the same literal.
rights	FRFX0X6	0x001200af
rights	0X1200AF	0x001200af

# A single mnemonic, and the composites they are built from.
rights	FR	0x00120089
rights	FW	0x00120116
rights	FX	0x001200a0
rights	FA	0x001f01ff

# Generic and standard rights.
rights	GA	0x10000000
rights	GR	0x80000000
rights	GW	0x40000000
rights	GX	0x20000000
rights	GRGX	0xa0000000
rights	SDRCWDWO	0x000f0000

# A hex literal that sets bits no mnemonic names.
rights	GA0x6	0x10000006
rights	0x0	0x00000000

# --- Rejected rights fields -----------------------------------------------

# A hex literal can only close a field: it consumes the rest of it, so
# anything after it is part of the literal and fails to parse as hex.
badrights	0x6FR
badrights	FR0x6FX
# An odd trailing character is not half a mnemonic.
badrights	FRF
# `0x` with nothing after it is not a hex literal, and not a mnemonic either.
badrights	0x
badrights	FR0x
# Not a mnemonic in anyone's table.
badrights	ZZ
badrights	FRZZ

# --- SID aliases ----------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every absolute alias in MS-DTYP §2.5.1.1. Domain- and machine-relative
# aliases (DA, DU, DG, DC, DD, CA, SA, EA, PA, CN, AP, KA, EK, RS, RO, LA, LG)
# are deliberately absent: they resolve only against a domain or machine SID,
# which Peios has no model for, so libpeios rejects them and libp-go needs an
# explicit WithDomain/WithMachine context. They are not a round trip.

# World, logon-type and creator principals.
sid	WD	S-1-1-0
sid	AN	S-1-5-7
sid	AU	S-1-5-11
sid	IU	S-1-5-4
sid	NU	S-1-5-2
sid	SU	S-1-5-6
sid	RC	S-1-5-12
sid	WR	S-1-5-33
sid	PS	S-1-5-10
sid	ED	S-1-5-9
sid	CO	S-1-3-0
sid	CG	S-1-3-1
sid	OW	S-1-3-4
sid	AC	S-1-15-2-1
sid	SY	S-1-5-18
sid	LS	S-1-5-19
sid	NS	S-1-5-20

# Integrity levels. S-1-16-0 (untrusted) and S-1-16-20480 (protected process)
# have no alias in MS-DTYP and are written in full by both sides.
sid	LW	S-1-16-4096
sid	ME	S-1-16-8192
sid	MP	S-1-16-8448
sid	HI	S-1-16-12288
sid	SI	S-1-16-16384

# The BUILTIN domain, S-1-5-32-*. Absolute despite the name: the RIDs are
# fixed by MS-DTYP, not allocated per machine.
sid	BA	S-1-5-32-544
sid	BU	S-1-5-32-545
sid	BG	S-1-5-32-546
sid	PU	S-1-5-32-547
sid	AO	S-1-5-32-548
sid	SO	S-1-5-32-549
sid	PO	S-1-5-32-550
sid	BO	S-1-5-32-551
sid	RE	S-1-5-32-552
sid	RU	S-1-5-32-554
sid	RD	S-1-5-32-555
sid	NO	S-1-5-32-556
sid	MU	S-1-5-32-558
sid	LU	S-1-5-32-559
sid	IS	S-1-5-32-568
sid	CY	S-1-5-32-569
sid	ER	S-1-5-32-573
sid	CD	S-1-5-32-574
sid	RA	S-1-5-32-575
sid	ES	S-1-5-32-576
sid	MS	S-1-5-32-577
sid	HA	S-1-5-32-578
sid	AA	S-1-5-32-579
sid	RM	S-1-5-32-580
